title: Users come back empty
prompt: Should return every user. Callers always get [].
explanation: forEach ignores the promises its callback returns, so loadAll returns before any fetch finishes. Map to promises and await them together.
hint: Which line starts async work that nothing waits for?

title: The catch never runs
prompt: When the request fails, logError never runs and the caller gets a rejected promise.
explanation: Returning a promise without await leaves the try block straight away. The rejection happens later, outside the try, so the catch never sees it. Inside try, write return await.
hint: When does the request actually fail, compared to when the function leaves the try block?

title: Inactive users get through
prompt: Should keep only active users. Returns every user.
fix:
const statuses = await Promise.all(users.map((u) => getStatus(u.id)));
return users.filter((_, i) => statuses[i] === 'active');
explanation: An async callback always returns a Promise, and a Promise is truthy, so filter keeps everything. Fetch all the statuses first, then filter synchronously.
hint: What does an async function return, and is that value truthy?

title: The counter never moves
explanation: A regular function gets its own this from how it's called, and the timer doesn't call it on your object. An arrow function has no this of its own, so it uses the one from start().
hint: Inside that callback, who decides what this is?

title: Every timer reads past the end
prompt: Throws TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name').
explanation: var is function-scoped, so every callback shares one i. By the time the timers fire, the loop has finished and i === tasks.length. let creates a fresh binding each iteration.
hint: How many separate copies of i exist?
